- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior-day trend.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., <0.3) and price falls, model often undercorrects; increase downward bias by 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 2–5% downward adjustment to initial values.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.5–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average before final output.
